issues.summary: Online revenue can be double-counted in Summary, and the phase's own remediation path recreates the duplicate. shopifyWeeklyPull writes a pull-owned Summary row (kind=revenue, supplier='shopify_orderapp', location='online') for the last 4 completed weeks, while weeklySummarize STILL derives a second online Summary row from any residual Revenue-tab channel='online' rows — aggregateSupplierRows_ (Code.gs:1670) groups them per source, upsertRows_ sees a different key and APPENDS alongside the pull row, and doGetSummary_ returns both rows for the week (consumers sum them). test_code.js case5 (line 4836) pins this coexistence as intended behaviour rather than detecting it. Two things make it more than theoretical: (a) greenBeanPull now calls weeklySummarize automatically for affected weeks up to 3 months back, so the legacy row is regenerated on a schedule, not only by the Monday trigger; (b) cleanupOnlineRevenueSummaryRows deletes the online SUMMARY rows but never the Revenue rows backing them, and the TODO runbook's own step 1 prescribes running that cleanup + runOnlineRevenueResummarize — which re-derives exactly the source-keyed online row that then doubles with the shopify_orderapp row. validateIngest_'s new rejection closes only the FUTURE POST path; docs/schema.md:97 concedes historical online Revenue rows exist. The only protection is the one-shot manual 'double-count sweep' probe in TODO step 7, which cannot catch a regeneration that happens weeks later. Cheap mechanical fix: have weeklySummarize_impl_ log (or raise the existing data-quality alert) when a week produces a non-shopify_orderapp online revenue group while a shopify_orderapp Summary row exists for the same week, and amend the runbook step so residual online Revenue rows are archived/relabelled rather than left to be re-derived.

greenBeanFetchAllRows_ silently ends paging when paging.truncated===true but paging.rowsIncluded is neither true nor false (absent, or a non-boolean). Neither the size-guard abort (requires rowsIncluded===false) nor the continue branch (requires ===true) matches, so the loop breaks, a PARTIAL window is ingested, orderAppRunSuccess_ stamps the heartbeat and the run reports success with no apiFailed and no log. The round-4 shape gate (line 532) only asserts meta.paging is an object; it does not type-check the two flags it then branches on. This is the same failure class the shopify side treats as a hard failure (shopifyValidWeekBody_ fails the week on ANY deviation). It requires the Order app to deviate from the step-4 contract, hence minor — but the fallout (silently understated committed spend, marked healthy) is the worst kind. Fix: treat truncated===true with a non-boolean rowsIncluded as an abort (return null) rather than a normal loop exit.

CARRIED from round 4, unfixed. Ambiguous response shape on the excluded-gross reconciliation signal: excluded.byStatusTotals.gross and excluded.cancelled.gross are read as objects each holding a scalar .gross. If the Order app actually returns byStatusTotals as a per-status map ({PENDING:{gross:N},...}), Number(undefined)||0 yields 0 and excludedGross stays 0 forever — a fail-open, fail-silent read of a money-reconciliation signal. Test case9 (test_code.js:4900) only exercises the assumed shape, and there is no log for the 'bucket present but unparseable' state (truthy object, non-numeric .gross), which is the only state that would reveal a mismatch. Cheap fix: log once when `excluded` is non-empty but weekExcluded computes to 0.

CARRIED from round 4, unfixed. orderAppRaiseDataQualityAlert_ has no threshold and no suppression: greenBeanPull raises an all-day Calendar event on EVERY run while any flagged intake row sits in the window. The window is a rolling 3 calendar months, so one un-fixed non-numeric 06_Stock_Intake cell produces ~13 consecutive weekly alerts. The function's own docstring reserves it for 'RARE, ACTIONABLE' states, and the sibling run-failure alert IS threshold-gated (ORDERAPP_ALERT_THRESHOLD=2) — the asymmetry makes this the alert most likely to be tuned out. Same applies to the upstream-warnings alert at line 553 (deduped per pull, not across pulls).
